compound_reference.match_rationale: The PubMed abstract names caffeine but does not report a structure identifier or Phase1B ID. The Phase1B-v1.3.1 registry contains the candidate record under this ID; the link is retained as a name-level cross-reference and is not identity-adjudicated.

research_question: In healthy young adults, do beverage vehicle (coffee versus energy drink), beverage temperature, or rapid versus slower consumption materially change caffeine pharmacokinetic profiles after the studied dose?

study.population_or_model: 24 healthy subjects aged 18-30 completed the study

conditions.dose_basis: administered dose stated in PubMed abstract; five conditions
conditions.preparation: Coffee or a sugar-free energy drink; coffee/energy drink temperature and consumption rate varied by condition
experimental_conditions: 10 serial plasma samples after each caffeine dose

outcome.measure: Plasma caffeine concentration-time profile and pharmacokinetic parameters
outcome.reported_result: The abstract reports similar mean concentration-time profiles with overlapping standard deviations at measured time points. An omnibus repeated-measures analysis found differences in mean Cmax and Vdss/F, but no pairwise comparison reached statistical significance; no numerical PK estimates are extracted here.
outcome.denominator: 24 participants completed; five crossover conditions; 10 serial plasma samples after each condition
outcome.uncertainty: The abstract reports overlapping standard deviations but provides no numerical estimates or confidence intervals for these outcomes.

identity_assessment.basis: The abstract identifies the analyte by the common name caffeine; no chemical identifier is reported in the source section reviewed.

applicability_assessment.food_matrix: Coffee and a sugar-free energy drink under the study protocols
applicability_assessment.preparation: Beverage temperature and consumption rate as specified in the abstract; serving composition and preparation details not extracted from full text
applicability_assessment.rationale: The result is restricted to a single administered dose and the tested beverage protocols. It cannot be generalized to other foods, recipes, populations, or doses without review of full methods and results.

limitations: Only the PubMed abstract was inspected for this extraction; full-text tables and figures were not reviewed.
The abstract does not provide the numerical Cmax, AUC, Tmax, or half-life values, so this record supports no numeric exposure conversion.
A single 160 mg administered dose and 24 healthy completers do not establish dose-response or applicability to other populations.
The source's common-name analyte identification is not an adjudicated chemical-identity crosswalk to Phase1B.
This record is contextual research evidence and is not a food concentration, cooking-retention factor, safety threshold, or clinical recommendation.

extraction.method: manual transcription and paraphrase from the NCBI PubMed abstract; no automated or LLM-generated acceptance
extraction.source_location: PubMed record PMID 27100333, Abstract: Materials, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion

review.reviewer_notes: Single-pass abstract-level extraction. Full text and independent source-level verification are pending.
review.decision_rationale: Not accepted for downstream calculation or contextual display pending independent review, full-text assessment, and identity/application adjudication.
